### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/knowledge-turso`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via vectorIndexThreshold (symbol, a field of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter; a field of interface KnowledgeTursoPluginOptions; a field of interface TursoKnowledgeAdapterOptions))_
- `content/docs/plugins/index.mdx`  _(via healthCheck (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via healthCheck (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via healthCheck (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via completeBuild (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter), dropSource (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter), healthCheck (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter), vectorIndexOverfetch (symbol, a field of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter; a field of interface KnowledgeTursoPluginOptions; a field of interface TursoKnowledgeAdapterOptions), vectorIndexThreshold (symbol, a field of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter; a field of interface KnowledgeTursoPluginOptions; a field of interface TursoKnowledgeAdapterOptions))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via healthCheck (symbol, a method of class TursoKnowledgeAdapter))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/README.md`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-turso/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d6db67f4c5b1ae1e6ffed4f55fe4f24c6e8706e8` — the merge of head `73d277418b303a87e50e4fd79592b6035f37fed5` into base `33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d6db67f4c5b1ae1e6ffed4f55fe4f24c6e8706e8 && git checkout d6db67f4c5b1ae1e6ffed4f55fe4f24c6e8706e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744 73d277418b303a87e50e4fd79592b6035f37fed5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744 && git merge --no-ff 73d277418b303a87e50e4fd79592b6035f37fed5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33a0d4fa625cdfb69873a89a1e0f5d9f49fea744` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c77819e170c953e0c32048b7c8209d2e07673d2c`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #37975 body and all four comments (triage 7220587871, claim 7226962676, dev report 7229320124, ruling A 7231124445); PR #38056 body, both comments, the ten-file net diff against the merge-base with `main`; the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run.

Check-runs as read on this head: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`, except one `Check Changeset` run `cancelled` beside two `success` runs of the same name. Still `in_progress` when read: `Test Core` shards 1 to 8 of 10, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`. This record does not judge green; the lane does.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface the diff implies, each named:

- **Two new optional options, `vectorIndexThreshold` and `vectorIndexOverfetch`, on `TursoKnowledgeAdapterOptions` and `KnowledgeTursoPluginOptions`.** Right, a widening. Neither name exists anywhere on `origin/main` (tree-wide grep, changesets and changelogs included), so neither is released.
- **Two new exports, `VECTOR_INDEX_THRESHOLD` (20000) and `VECTOR_INDEX_OVERFETCH` (40).** Right, a widening.
- **`RangeError` for `vectorIndexOverfetch` that is not a whole number of 8 or more (ruling A, item 4).** Right, and not a narrowing: the option is new in this PR and in no release, so no caller on `main` or on any published version can pass a value that is now refused. The minimum follows the floor correctly: the in-scope pool can never exceed `topK × vectorIndexOverfetch`, and the leg's answer stands only at a pool of `8 × topK` or more, so a value under 8 could never answer approximately and would only add the one-bit scan to every search. At exactly 8 the approximate answer stands only when every candidate is in scope, which is coherent. Settled: 8 holds.
- **`RangeError` for `vectorIndexThreshold` that is NaN or under 1; `Infinity` accepted.** Right, new option, same reasoning.
- **Default behavior change: above 20,000 passages of one organization, after the next complete build, the vector leg ranks through the one-bit index.** Right, and stated plainly in the changeset (default named, recall 0.998 against the exact scan named, "keeps the exact scan until its next complete build"). Ruled on by the maintainer (ruling A, item 1). Not a narrowing of what a caller could rely on:
  - Score semantics are unchanged. The score is still the reciprocal rank fusion of the two legs' ranks 1 to topK, normalized into (0, 1]; `KnowledgeHitSchema` describes the score as adapter-specific, higher is better, normalised to [0, 1] when feasible. The approximate leg re-ranks by the stored float32 vector with the same order and the same cut at a cosine distance of 1, so a rank means what it meant.
  - Hit membership may differ from the exact scan (approximate by design). The published spec promises no exact nearest-neighbour membership; only this package's README did, and the README is rewritten in the same diff.
  - Hit count never drops: the approximate answer stands only when the vector leg ranks topK hits; otherwise the exact statement runs.
- **New refusal: an object the store did not make under `knowledge_SOURCE_gN-vec`, `-org` or a `-vec-*` trigger name now refuses `completeBuild`, `dropSource` and the opening of a generation with `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.** Judged right and not arm-changing: the names are hyphenated names beside the store's own passage table, which no source, generation or object name can hold, the same rule `main` already applies to the keyword-index names, and the changeset states it. nit: the PR body's sentence "nothing that was accepted before is refused" is not literally true for this one hand-made-object case; say so there.
- **`healthCheck()` message.** `ok` stays true; the message is unchanged when the index works and gains notes otherwise. Right.

Tenancy (rule: the candidates are ranked before the filter, so an index is never used over more than one organization, per passage table):

- Build: the organization count is read inside the same transaction that makes the index DDL; more than one organization (no organization counts as one more) commits the organization index alone and no side table. Holds.
- A later write of a second organization's passage: the organization count is read from the passage table at every search that would take the index, never cached. Holds.
- Search: both statements, approximate and exact, carry the identical in-scope `WHERE` (organization, record scope, metadata filter) with the same bound values, the keyword leg is unchanged, and the final join reads only chunk ids the legs produced. The exact fallback therefore cannot return a passage out of scope, and neither can the approximate statement, whatever the organization count is. Holds.
- Scoped-recall floor and short-leg re-run: the approximate answer stands only when the in-scope pool is `8 × topK` or more AND the vector leg ranks `topK` hits; an empty result reads as pool 0 and re-runs exactly. Holds, and the floor is pinned by the over-fetch test (ablation 4).
- N1 (nit) — rule level: the per-search organization read and the search statement are two statements, not one transaction. Isolation does not depend on the pair being atomic (the `WHERE` enforces it) and recall is covered by the floor, so the rule "never used over two organizations" is held up to that window, not absolutely.
- S1 (should-fix) — rule level: the "this table's index is complete" fact is remembered per process and is invalidated only by that process's own drops. The README sentence "a side table short of its passage table is never searched" and the fallback to the exact scan therefore hold within one process, not across the processes the README says may share a store. No out-of-scope passage can result; a failed or thin search can.

Hosted DDL guard (ruling A, item 3):

- A database that does not compute one-bit vectors: probed before any DDL; no object is made; the build completes; the source keeps the exact scan. Holds, pinned (`ann_no_1bit`).
- A refused DDL transaction rolls back whole; the build completes on the exact scan. Holds, pinned (`ann_no_ddl`, ablation 6).
- A refused copy batch ends the copy; the side table's count differs from the passage table's, so it is not searched; the build completes. Holds by reading. S2 (should-fix) — this half is not pinned by a test of its own. Both pinned variants stop before the copy runs, and ruling A item 3 says "a refused index or backfill ... pinned". Add a variant that accepts the DDL and refuses the `INSERT ... SELECT` batch.
- `healthCheck()` names the missing one-bit vectors for the whole store, and each refused source with its reason. Holds, pinned. N2 (nit) — the per-source record is process memory. It is lost on restart and is not seen by another process (for example a server whose index was refused during a CLI rebuild) until that process's own next complete build; the README's "until a later build makes the index" reads as durable.

Other findings:

- S3 (should-fix) — every vector search of a passage table without a complete index now adds two catalog reads (`sqlite_master` and `pragma_table_info`) before the search statement, including for every source under the threshold and when `vectorIndexThreshold` is `Infinity`. On a hosted database that is two more round trips per search for deployments that get nothing from the index, and neither the changeset nor the README says so. Skip the read when the threshold is `Infinity`, and remember a negative answer for a bounded time or until this process's next complete build.
- S4 (should-fix) — unverified on hosted: the candidate count is bound for both statements, but the exact statement does not use it. When the query yields no keyword term (punctuation only) it is a trailing unused positional value. The local stores accept that (the suite ran green locally per the PR body); whether a hosted server refuses a surplus positional value was not checked. Bind it only for the approximate statement, or have the requested hosted check include a term-less query.

Docs, README and changeset against the code: the thresholds, the 2,048-row batches, the `topK × vectorIndexOverfetch` candidates, the `8 × topK` floor, the short-leg re-run, the per-search organization read, the object names, the drops by a switch and by `dropSource`, and the two options all match. Measured numbers are the dev's and were not re-measured. N3 (nit) — `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` still says "an exact scan by cosine distance" in the Search bullet of section 4.2 and "exact scan" in the `knowledge-turso` row of the adapter table near line 1306.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/knowledge-turso-approximate-index.md`: `@objectstack/knowledge-turso` at `patch`. Correct: a non-protocol change ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, changeset rule), and the diff moves no other package.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: true. Two options and two exports are added; no export, option or accepted value on `main` is removed or refused; the one new minimum is on an option this PR introduces. The line is identical in the PR body and the changeset.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: true. Both options are constructor options in code; nothing a metadata author writes changes, and no file under `packages/spec` is in the diff.
- No BREAKING banner is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (one-bit side table in place of `libsql_vector_idx`): answered by ruling A in 7231124445, option A, on by default.
- open_questions 2 (organization rule per passage table or store-wide): answered by ruling A item 5, per passage table.
- Deviation "Clause-② declared yes (widening), the claim said no": correct on the final diff, see ②.
- Deviations "tests and gates not measured under the lock" (head 19841efaf2): superseded by the PR body's lock-held runs on c77819e170; the head's check-runs are still in progress, see the top of this record.
- Ruling item 2 (scoped-recall pin, real-store rows at 10% and 20% in the PR body): present (rows at 10%, 15% and 20%; the scoped-recall test and the over-fetch test).
- Ruling item 6 (follow-up card for a second approximate attempt on narrow scopes): the PR body says it is to be filed; no card number is given in the body. The area reports it filed as #38066; the body should name it.
- The hosted check asked of the cloud seat is non-blocking by the ruling; not answered when read.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. Candidate selection, the in-scope filter, the float32 re-rank, the pool count and the backfill (`INSERT ... SELECT`, keyset batches) all run in SQL; no id set is materialised in the application and no join is done in-app.

Open on this head: S1, S2, S3 and S4 (cross-process index-complete memory; a pin for a refused copy batch; the per-search catalog reads; the surplus bound value on a term-less exact search). Each earns a delta review of its fix. N4 (nit) — the PR body's "nothing that was accepted before is refused" is slightly too strong: a foreign object under one of the store's new hyphenated names is now refused, as the changeset states. Nits N1 to N4 are optional.

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK** at head `c77819e170c953e0c32048b7c8209d2e07673d2c` (Fixes #37975, ruling A 7231124445).

## Review summary

**Face.** The face is declaration (TIER_DEFAULT): there is no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed rule text and no narrowing. Ruling item 4 is settled. `vectorIndexOverfetch` and `vectorIndexThreshold` are new in this PR: neither appears on `main` or in any released changeset or changelog. A minimum born with the option narrows nothing. The minimum of 8 follows the floor, because the in-scope pool can never exceed `topK × overfetch` and the approximate answer stands only at a pool of `8 × topK` or more. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `patch` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right. Score semantics stay within `KnowledgeHitSchema`'s description. The PR stays Tier S.

**Contract review.** Declaration record 7231688504 has no must-fix. It does have four graded should-fix findings, S1 to S4, so the queue guard reads them as open on this head. Each needs its fix and a delta read.
- **S1:** the index-complete memory is per process and is not invalidated by another process's drop and rebuild, while the README says several processes may share a store. No passage out of scope can result, but a search in another process can fail or rank thin. The mechanism goes to the area privately.
- **S2:** ruling item 3 asks for a pin on a refused backfill. Both pinned variants stop before the copy runs. Add a variant that accepts the DDL and refuses a copy batch.
- **S3:** every vector search of a table without a complete index adds two catalog reads. That includes sources under the threshold and `vectorIndexThreshold: Infinity`, so a hosted store pays two more round trips for nothing. Skip the read in those cases, and either state the remaining cost or remember the answer.
- **S4:** the candidate count is bound for the exact statement too, where a term-less query leaves it as a surplus positional value. Bind it only where used, or have the hosted check include a term-less query.

**What holds.** Tenancy holds on the build, on a later second-organization write and on the search. The approximate and exact statements share the identical in-scope `WHERE` and bound values, so neither returns a passage out of scope. The scoped-recall floor and the short-leg exact re-run hold. A refused index keeps the exact scan, and the build completes. `healthCheck` names the cause.

**Nits, optional:**
- N1: the organization read and the search are two statements.
- N2: the refusal record is process memory.
- N3: two leftover "exact scan" sentences in `knowledge.mdx`.
- N4: the body overstates "nothing accepted before is refused".

The body should also name follow-up #38066 for ruling item 6.

**Gates.** CI was still running at this reading. The next head needs every check green.

**Next:** fix S1 to S4. Then a delta declaration record and a delta L1 follow, and the area lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `50e245a081eaf109a3bc9e3d7f1717e2332f50e7`
Local-runs: none

Delta round on the record in comment 7231688504 (head c77819e170), which left S1 to S4 open. Face unchanged: declaration, plus the published option surface.

Read: the first-parent moves c77819e170 to 50e245a081 (f5d171e4dc main merge, 98ffbe4340, b113f0830f, 50e245a081 main merge); the author delta `git diff 98ffbe4340^ b113f0830f` (five files); the net diff against the merge-base with `main` at the head; PR body v3; the PR comments; card #37975 comments; issue #38066; the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run.

Check-runs on this head, read at 04:44Z: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`. Still `in_progress`: `Test Core` shards 1 to 10, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`. This record does not judge green; the lane does.

Not found when read: the area's announcement comment on the PR and a new dev report on #37975. The PR thread holds the docs-drift comment, the two review claims, the earlier record and the L1 verdict; the card still holds its four earlier comments. The PR body v3 was read in their place.

### ① Derived judgments

Closures of the earlier findings:

S1 (should-fix): closed

The index memory is keyed per generation instance, with a catch backstop on the approximate statement. Pinned by two acceptance tests. The backstop runs the exact statement, which carries the same in-scope `WHERE`.

S2 (should-fix): closed

A third refusal variant, `ann_no_copy`, accepts the index DDL and refuses the copy batch. It pins that the build completes, the index objects are there and short of the passage table, the search runs the exact scan, and the health check names the source with "the database refused its copy". Ruling A item 3 is now pinned in both halves.

S3 (should-fix): closed

At `vectorIndexThreshold: Infinity` a search reads no catalog for an index. Otherwise a process reads it once per generation instance and remembers the answer either way; a build records what it found for its own process. Pinned (under the threshold, at `Infinity`, a second adapter that did not build the source). The cost that remains is stated in the README and the PR body: an index another process completes inside the active generation is used after this process's next complete build of the source, or a restart.

S4 (should-fix): closed

The candidate count is bound for the approximate statement alone, after every other value; the exact statement binds exactly the values it reads. Pinned by a test of a query without a keyword term.

Earlier nits: N3 (the health check's refusal record is process memory) is closed by a README sentence and a PR-body line. N4 (the PR body's "nothing accepted before is refused") is closed: the Clause-② paragraph now names the one exception, the refusal of a hand-made object under a `-vec`, `-org` or `-vec-*` name, as the rule `main` already applies to the keyword-index names. The docs nit is closed: the Search bullet of section 4.2 and the `knowledge-turso` row of the adapter table now name the vector leg as an exact scan or the approximate index. The tenancy nit (the per-search organization read and the search statement are not one transaction) stands as a nit; isolation is held by the shared `WHERE`.

Public surface in the delta: none added, none removed. No export, option, default or accepted value moves. One behavior is now defined where it was not: at `Infinity` an index made earlier under a finite threshold is no longer searched. That agrees with the option's documented meaning (it turns the index off) and refuses nothing.

Tenancy, re-read on the delta: the organization count is still read from the passage table at every search that would take the index and is not part of the remembered answer; a remembered "complete" alone never admits the index. The backfill's still-here check now also matches the generation row's creation time. Holds.

The two main merges: f5d171e4dc changes none of the PR's ten files. 50e245a081 changes two of them, `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx` (one hunk near line 304) and `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx` (hunks near lines 351, 926 and 1143), all outside the PR's own hunks. The net diff at the head shows the PR's hunks intact: one in `knowledge-rag.mdx` (the libSQL search bullet) and three in `knowledge.mdx` (the section 4.2 opening, the Search and Approximate index bullets, the adapter table row).

Changeset and docs, sentence by sentence against the code:

- Changeset, new sentence "A process reads the catalog for a generation's index once (two reads) and remembers the answer; at `vectorIndexThreshold: Infinity` it never does." True for searches. nit: a complete build still reads the catalog at any threshold, `Infinity` included, to refuse a foreign object; the README says "a search never reads", which is the exact form.
- Changeset, unchanged sentences: re-read, still match (threshold, one organization, `topK × vectorIndexOverfetch`, the `8 × topK` floor and the short-leg re-run, the 2,048-row batches, the names, the drops, the two options, the minimum of 8).
- README "A copy batch the database refuses ends the copy the same way ...": matches; the build forgets its memory when the copy ends or is refused, and the next search finds the counts differ.
- README "The health check's record of a refusal is kept by the process that ran the build, until it restarts.": matches.
- README "What a search reads to choose": each sentence matches (two catalog reads on first search of an instance; keyed by number and row creation time; a build remembers for its own process; `Infinity`; another process's index; three seeks of the organization index).
- `knowledge.mdx` Search bullet and table row: match.
- nit: no page says that at `Infinity` an index made earlier is left in place, kept in step by its triggers, and not searched.

PR body v3, the new lines: the S1 to S4 paragraphs match the code as closed above; the operator sentence on `healthCheck()` is now correct (a named source runs the exact scan for that refusal; an unnamed one may still run it for another reason); the measured runs are the dev's and were not re-measured.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `@objectstack/knowledge-turso` at `patch`; `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, identical in the PR body and the changeset. The delta adds no surface and narrows nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Ruling A item 6: answered. Follow-up #38066 is open ("a scoped vector search under the 8 x topK floor tries a second, wider approximate pass before the exact scan"), labelled `area:ai`, `priority:p3`, `pm:blocked`, and the PR body names it.
- Ruling A item 3: now pinned for the index and the backfill (S2).
- The hosted check asked of the cloud seat is non-blocking by the ruling; not answered when read.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding in the delta. The remembered answer replaces repeated catalog reads; no id set is materialised and no join moves into the application.

Open after this round: three nits (the changeset's `Infinity` sentence, the unstated fate of an earlier index at `Infinity`, the two-statement organization read).

No must-fix, no should-fix.
